scope: Xbox-facing platform libraries reviewed during Frosty bring-up, including the input, audio and media providers reached through the host. Coverage describes translation of console interfaces. Package middleware and ordinary Win32 dependencies are inventoried separately.

levels.complete: All identified console exports and interfaces for the reviewed build have an implemented, behaviorally verified replacement.
levels.partial: A TuxBox provider or named reference bridge implements at least one verified Xbox-facing behavior. Other exports, interface methods or execution paths remain open.
levels.incomplete: The baseline has no verified replacement for this library's Xbox-specific behavior. Tests may exercise the original binary or the host implementation.

libraries.name: d3d12_xs.dll
libraries.provider: TuxBox Rust device and command providers with desktop D3D12 root-signature serialization.
libraries.scope: Two Xbox device profiles, eight feature queries, GPU heaps, guest-backed textures, queues, indirect compute, direct and indirect mesh dispatch, descriptor and query operations, and 32 identifiers. Frosty creates 680-byte mesh pipelines and 712-byte graphics pipelines through ID3D12Device2 and presents 3840 × 2160 frames. A fresh Proton prefix running the checkout-built providers displays the menu and video preview, opens Settings and enters the Wake Up sequence. GPU tests cover indexed draws, depth/stencil writes, NV12 plane copies, and whole and regional copies into a tiled RGBA8 texture with guest-memory writeback and alias readback. The framebuffer-preservation size getter matches the supplied DLL in its initial state.
libraries.remaining: Six PE functions, additional Xbox interface methods and pipeline subobjects, and more retail shaders remain open. Guest-backed color textures still need render-target and UAV writes. Using distinct overlapping layouts in the same GPU write batch remains unsupported. Virtual-memory configuration accepts no valid requests yet; the initial framebuffer-size check does not cover a configured state.

export_coverage.notes: Fifteen of 22 functions and all 32 data exports have verified behavior. The original DLL returns DXGI_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED for four legacy DXGIX exports. Rendering coverage is tracked through separate device and command-list tests. D3D12ZeroMemoryX was checked in CPU mode.

inventory.file_description: Xbox D3D12.XS Runtime Library for Xbox Extensions

libraries.name: dxcompiler_xs.dll
libraries.provider: TuxBox PE forwarder to desktop DXC.
libraries.scope: Both SDK factories create a desktop DXC utility object through the Xbox DLL. Tests check blob contents, lifetime and use of a caller-supplied allocator.
libraries.remaining: The console ray-tracing factories CreateXdxrCompiler and CreateXdxrCompiler2 remain unimplemented.

libraries.name: xmem.dll
libraries.provider: TuxBox Rust CPU memory provider.
libraries.scope: Nine exports cover heap allocation, working-set statistics, virtual memory, and the CPU side of the title’s 64 KiB physical-page profile. The guest preserves 131,072 bytes across unmap and remap in reversed page order. XMemMakeTag matches the supplied routine on 5,120 inputs. XMemVirtualQuery explicitly reports unsupported pending a verified Xbox success path. Allocation and free calls route through installed callbacks; a local reference control checks argument forwarding and restoring defaults. XMemGetWriteWatch and XMemResumeWriteWatch match the checked suspension transitions and host dirty-page query. The checked write-watch allocation profiles are exercised end-to-end on the CPU. Scatter mapping supports provider-owned CPU pages with remapping and guard checks. Profile 1 accepts checked CPU reserve/commit and ordinary protection combinations. Ordinary CPU heap routing covers the tested attribute fields, including zero.
libraries.remaining: GPU-visible backing, concurrent aliases, the Xbox partition allocator, additional allocation profiles and retail validation remain open. XMemVirtualQuery console metadata and success-path reference comparison remain open. Memory profiling callbacks and concurrent guest callback lifetime remain unverified. Other XMemSetOption IDs and untested Xbox allocation profiles remain unsupported; console concurrency has not been compared. Scatter mapping has not been compared against the console NT success path and does not support GPU backing or simultaneous aliases. Xbox partition heap, special alignment and allocation-failure behavior remain unverified.

export_coverage.notes: The physical-page controls validate CPU data and ownership for flags 0x20400000. The packaged DLL could not initialize xbthunk on either Proton build.

libraries.name: xg_xs.dll
libraries.provider: TuxBox texture address computer.
libraries.scope: Computes linear and 4 KiB tiled 2D textures, array slices and packed mip chains. TuxBox and the supplied DLL matched on 9,231,018 texel or block addresses across 78 formats and 156 layouts. A separate check includes eight descriptors from Frosty. XGComputeBufferLayout matches the supplied DLL on 967 buffer descriptors, including invalid arguments and full output guards. The 2D-specific layout and computer exports match the supplied DLL on 7,020 sampled layouts and 81,432 sampled addresses for the checked usage and swizzle profiles. The 1D-specific layout and computer exports match 4,104 sampled linear layouts and 45,144 addresses for 57 uncompressed formats. The 3D-specific layout and computer exports match 12,825 sampled linear layouts and 99,180 sampled addresses for 57 uncompressed formats. Tile shapes for buffers and checked 2D formats matched the supplied DLL across 11,990 cases. Depth/stencil swizzle validation matched the supplied DLL across 6,125 cases. Optimal swizzle selection matches the supplied DLL across 70,200 cases; the eight-argument ABI is confirmed at two supplied driver call sites.
libraries.remaining: Further formats and tiling modes, tiled 3D textures, multisampling and subresource copies. Calling an unimplemented texture computer method terminates the guest. Other 2D-specific descriptor profiles return unsupported. Block-compressed and other untested 1D descriptor profiles return unsupported. Compressed 3D textures, depth-only mip chains and other untested 3D profiles return unsupported. Tile shapes for 1D and 3D match the sampled reference rejections; unknown formats remain unsupported. Other SDK versions and source-level defaults for the eighth argument are unverified.

libraries.name: xgameruntime.dll
libraries.provider: TuxBox Xbox Game Runtime with Rust task queues.
libraries.scope: TuxBox implements runtime initialization, threading-interface queries and queues. The guest checks manual, threadpool, serialized and immediate dispatch, cancellation and termination.
libraries.remaining: User and device association, storage and other service interfaces remain open. The error-report export has no behavior control.

export_coverage.notes: Four entry points have guest behavior checks. QueryApiImpl currently serves the threading interface. The export count excludes interface methods.

libraries.remaining: BCPack, swizzled or physical-page requests, console-specific storage controls and scheduling priorities.

export_coverage.notes: The factory is the sole static XCRDAPI import in this Frosty executable.

libraries.name: gameconfighelper.dll

libraries.scope: Implements three of the 24 exports in the reviewed Windows Game Runtime helper. libraries.remaining: The embedded runtime's GetCurrentPackageGameConfig call and the remaining configuration and package-identity queries.

libraries.name: GameInput.dll
libraries.provider: TuxBox GameInput v0 provider for polling and device status callbacks.

libraries.remaining: Reading callbacks, text translation, wheel input, haptics and additional device types remain open. Hardware controller behavior needs a physical-device check.

export_coverage.notes: The singleton factory and a subset of its returned interface are exercised. The one-export denominator excludes COM methods.
